title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from p.44: V is a real 2-dimensional vector space. A finite dihedral group D of order 2m acts on V, and J̃ indexes m = 2n vectors R̃_j forming a regular m-gon; the figure shows a hexagon, so m = 6 and n = 3. The central element a_0 = -1 is the unique element of order 2 in the rotation subgroup D^+. Grothendieck has also made V Euclidean with the unique D-invariant quadratic form equal to 1 on the R̃_j.

What this page does:
(10) He complexifies and takes the complex projective line Σ = P(V_C) = (V_C \ 0)/C^*. This is a Riemann sphere whose real points Σ_R = P(V) form a circle. He also names it Σ_{J̃}(C), viewing it as an object attached to the dihedral datum J̃.
- D acts on Σ with kernel exactly the centre {1, a_0}. So the effective action is by D' = D/{1, a_0}, which is dihedral of order 2n (D_n).
- R_i denotes the image of R̃_i in Σ. Antipodal vectors span the same line, so R_i = R_{a_0(i)}. The set of R_i is therefore naturally indexed by J = J̃/{1, a_0}, a set with n elements.
- Result: an n-pointed real sphere (Σ, J ⊂ Σ_R ⊂ Σ) whose points lie on the real circle in a dihedral cyclic order, with symmetry group D_n.
- In the coordinate z = (x+iy)/(x−iy), Σ_R becomes the unit circle and the R_i become the n-th roots of unity. D'^+ acts as z ↦ ζz and reflections act as z ↦ 1/z (up to conjugation).

The slanted marginal NB, mostly illegible, seems to say that (Σ, J ⊂ Σ) is determined up to unique isomorphism by the dihedral structure on J. It also seems to discuss how the D-action descends via D'.

Next page (14)-(15): D'^+ has exactly two fixed points, the isotropic eigenlines of the rotations, i.e. the circular points. They are the two 'poles' P_ω, one in each hemisphere of Σ \ Σ_R. These hemispheres are indexed by the orientations of Σ_R.

Purpose: in a manuscript on Teichmüller groupoids of type (0,n), this builds a canonical, maximally symmetric base point of M_{0,n} for each dihedral structure on an n-element set J. It is the centre of the corresponding real cell (associahedron) of M_{0,n}(R). It comes with two canonical extra points (the poles) and an action of D_n. Presumably it serves as a base point, or base 'tangential' datum, for the Teichmüller groupoid, functorial in the dihedral structure.
errors: V_C^*/C^* should be read as (V_C minus 0)/C^*; this is a notational shorthand, not an error.
The next page speaks of fixed points of D' on Σ. Strictly, only D'^+ fixes the two poles, since reflections exchange them. Grothendieck's (15) does correctly use Σ^{D^+}.
In the illustrated case n = 3, the configuration has no moduli. That is harmless but uninformative.

ideas.what: Complexify a real dihedral configuration to get the Riemann sphere P(V_C), with D acting through D/{±1}.
ideas.modern_name: PGL_2 action of a dihedral group; regular n-gon configuration on P^1

ideas.what: n points on the real circle P(V), images of a regular 2n-gon, indexed by J = J̃/{±1}; these are the n-th roots of unity in a suitable coordinate.
ideas.modern_name: most symmetric point of a real cell of M_{0,n}(R), with dihedral ordering (associahedron centre)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; dihedral structures on M_{0,n}(R) studied by Kapranov, Devadoss, Brown (dihedral coordinates)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller tower base points and symmetric configurations, but not this explicit construction as far as known

ideas.what: Canonical attachment of the pointed sphere (Σ, J) to an abstract dihedral structure, functorially, as a base-point device for Teichmüller groupoids.
ideas.modern_name: canonical base points / tangential base points indexed by dihedral structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara; Drinfeld; Brown for dihedral M_{0,n}

missed.claim: Grothendieck chooses base points for genus 0 Teichmüller groupoids canonically from a dihedral structure on the marked set. He uses the regular configuration together with its two D_n-fixed poles (circular points), indexed by orientations of Σ_R. This adds two canonical extra points to the n marked points, i.e. a link with M_{0,n+2} and the cyclotomic/roots-of-unity picture.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precursor of dihedral base-point choices (Brown's dihedral coordinates, the associahedral cell). It is mildly interesting as documentation, but the mathematics is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary and classical construction (regular n-points on P^1 with D_n symmetry); of interest only as documentation of Grothendieck's base-point setup for Teichmüller groupoids.
